text.div:
SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD

  • Medical oncology (genitourinary) consultation within two weeks for suspected metastatic prostate cancer: diagnosis, staging, systemic treatment, radiotherapy, bone health and genetic testing
  • Diagnosis and staging: multiparametric MRI of the prostate, an MRI-targeted transperineal biopsy at the urology practice, CT of the chest, abdomen and pelvis, a bone scan, and PSMA PET/CT
  • Bone pain: acetaminophen 1000 mg up to three times a day; spinal cord compression warning signs explained in Spanish, with same-day assessment for new leg weakness or numbness, or loss of bladder or bowel control
  • Care in Spanish, his first language: a professional medical interpreter for every major discussion, written plans in Spanish, appointments placed around his morning writing and his official duties
  • Systemic therapy: apalutamide 240 mg daily from the consultation day and leuprolide 22.5 mg every twelve weeks from one week later, continuous; docetaxel not added for low-volume disease
  • Radiotherapy to the prostate, 55 Gy in 20 daily fractions, about six weeks after starting androgen deprivation, for low-volume metastatic disease
  • Germline genetic testing with pre-test counseling, and somatic testing of the biopsy tissue
  • Bone health on androgen deprivation: DXA and FRAX, cholecalciferol 1945 units a day, calcium 1000 to 1200 mg a day from food, weight-bearing exercise, a dental examination, then denosumab 60 mg every six months for high fracture risk; DXA again in one to two years
  • Monitoring on androgen deprivation and apalutamide: PSA and testosterone every three months, blood count and chemistry, TSH every four months, blood pressure at every visit, hemoglobin A1c and lipids, rash, falls, hot flashes, sexual health, fatigue, mood and cognition
  • Apalutamide rash: triamcinolone 0.1% cream twice daily for two weeks, cetirizine 10 mg daily, fragrance-free emollient, continue apalutamide; stop it and call the same day for blisters, peeling, mouth or eye sores, fever, or spread beyond a third of the skin
  • Atorvastatin 20 mg daily for primary prevention, with a lipid panel and ALT in six to twelve weeks

resource.title: Pablo Neruda synthetic care plan
resource.description: De novo metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer in a 66-year-old Chilean poet and diplomat posted abroad, on the NCCN prostate cancer guideline, the AUA/SUO advanced prostate cancer guideline and the CMID prostate cancer monograph. Urinary symptoms and bone pain with a hard prostate and a raised PSA lead to MRI, an MRI-targeted biopsy, conventional staging (CT and bone scan) and PSMA PET/CT; the disease is classified as low volume, and the choice is continuous androgen deprivation with apalutamide plus radiotherapy to the prostate, without docetaxel. The episode covers flare protection, early PSA response and the three-month PSA, germline and somatic testing, bone health (DXA, FRAX, vitamin D, calcium, exercise, a dental check and denosumab at the osteoporosis dose), the cardiometabolic risks of androgen deprivation, apalutamide's drug interaction with amlodipine, its rash and its effect on thyroid function, hot flashes, sexual health, fatigue, mood, and care in Spanish, his first language, around his writing and diplomatic work. His documented prostate cancer, operated on in France in July 1916 while he was ambassador, frames the episode; the dispute over his death two years later is history only.
